To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mechanical load triggers the differentiation of subchondral bone cells via activation of the JUN/AP-1/RunX2 signaling pathway, and this is an early event in the remodeling of the mandibular subcondyle.
the mechanical load triggers differentiation of subchondral cells via the activation of the JUNK-c-Jun signaling pathway and c-Fos, as well as ERK/MAP kinase and the expression of Runx2.

mechanical loading induces differentiation phenomena through the activation of the Jnk/c-Jun and ERK/MAP kinase pathways and the expression of the transcription factors c-fos and runx2 in the subchandral bone of the mandibular head.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the mechanisms of bone remodeling, and in particular with the identification of the signaling pathways that are activated in response to functional loading of the condylar cartilaginous growth plate.
the elucidation of the signaling pathways involved in the mechano-transducing events in the subchandral bone area of the mandibular conydlar region.
the identification of the mechanisms that control the differentiation of the osteoblastic lineage and the possible interconnections with the condylar cartilaginous tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the JNK-AP-1 and ERK-MAPK signaling pathways are involved in the mechano-transduced events that lead to the activation of Runx2 and subsequent bone formation in the mandibular subchondral bone.
functional load triggers a cascade of events in subchondrial bone that involves the JNK-c-jun signaling pathway and the transcription factor c-fos.

functional loading of the condylar cartilaginous surface induces a mechano-transductive response that is transmitted through the subchondra to the underlying bone, which involves activation of the Jnk-c-Jun signaling pathway and c-Fos expression, as well as ERK and Runx2 activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical load is sensed by the cells in the condylar cartilaginous area and that the signaling events are transduced to the subchondoral area where the bone remodeling process occurs.

the JNK-c-Fos-AP-1-Runx2 signaling axis is activated in subchondoral osteoblasts in response to mechanical stimuli, thus providing an insight into the molecular events underlying bone remodeling in response to altered functional loading.
the JNK/Runx2 pathway is involved in the regulation of osteoblast differentiation in subchondra under functional load.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mechanical loading of the TMJ induces the expression of master tissue regulators and the activation of key signaling pathways in the osteoblasts of the subchondrial bone.

mechanical stimuli are sensed in subchondrial osteoblasts by the activation of a JNK-c-Fos signaling cascade and the subsequent activation of the ERK/MAPk pathway, leading to the expression of the transcriptional regulator Runx2.
the JNK/Runx2 axis may be a potential target for therapeutic interventions aimed at preventing or reversing bone loss in the mandibular subcondylar area.
